title: 2005 AMC 10B Problem 14
statement: Equilateral \(\triangle ABC\) has side length \(2,\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AC},\) and \(C\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{BD}.\) What is the area of \(\triangle CDM?\)

solutions.text:
Take \(\overline{CD}\) as the base. Since \(C\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{BD}\) and \(BC = 2,\) we have \(CD = 2.\)

The height of \(\triangle CDM\) is the distance from \(M\) to line \(BD.\) Because \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AC},\) this distance is half the height of \(\triangle ABC,\) which is \(\dfrac12 \cdot \sqrt3 = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}.\)

The area is \[ \dfrac12 \cdot 2 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}. \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Take \(\overline{CD}\) as the base; it has length \(2\)
The height from \(M\) to line \(BD\) is half the height of \(\triangle ABC\)
